newsitem.title: PERU: Aoki's wife retrieves photos from Peru siege site.
newsitem.headline: Aoki's wife retrieves photos from Peru siege site.

text.p: The wife of Japanese ambassador Morihisa Aoki went home for the first time in more than four months on Friday and found three treasured photos that survived Peru's explosive hostage drama.

Naoko Aoki dashed in through the front door of the wrecked residence and emerged several minutes later clutching three silver-framed portraits of Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and Emperor Akihito and his wife.
The photos appeared to have come through the 18-week hostage siege, which ended on Tuesday when crack troops stormed the building to free 71 hostages from Marxist rebels.

Aoki, who had not been home since 14 guerrillas crashed into a Dec. 17 cocktail held in honour of Emperor Akihito's 68th birthday, also grabbed a few articles of clothing, still on their hangers, which she slung over one arm.

The impromtu recovery of lost belongings occurred during a tour of the residence by Peru's President Alberto Fujimori, Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda and Ambassador Aoki, who was pushed around the grounds in a wheelchair after being injured during the rescue.

Modelled on Tara, the antebellum home in "Gone with the Wind," the colonnaded mansion in the upscale San Isidro district is now a burned-out shell, littered with the debris of Tuesday's raid that freed all but one of the 72 hostages.

Aoki was wheeled around to the side of the building to inspect the outside steps down which he and 70 other hostages were evacuated by elite troops three days ago. He beamed when his wife handed him the photos and proudly thrust the one of Hashimoto above his head to show cameras.
